_note: Margaret Teyl, party secretary. She speaks in text only and appears rarely: when you cross a line. At most once every two months. 'Agree' raises her loyalty; 'dismiss' lowers it. If her loyalty falls below 25 she leaves the party. New triggers: hypocrisy (a speech against the people whose money the party takes), deny (denying a scandal that's true), scapegoat (a colleague paid to take the fall; she always speaks then). Agreeing with her about money or hypocrisy makes her keep the books for a year (money secrets leak half as often); doing it again after agreeing costs much more of her loyalty.

flip: You said the opposite of what you said in spring. People keep cuttings, you know. So do I.
That's a different position from the one on our posters. Either change the posters or change your mind back.
against_manifesto: That's not what our manifesto says. If we're changing our minds, the party should hear it from you, not from the evening news.
Our members knocked on doors for the other side of that argument. I'd like to be able to tell them why.
dirty_money: I've seen where that money came from. When it comes out, and it will, I won't be the one explaining it.
We said we weren't for sale. That donor clearly thinks we are.
provocative_gaffe: That line will follow you for years. Some of our people had to apologise on your behalf today.
You can be angry without being cruel. The voters know the difference, even when the cameras don't.
steer: You're moving the party. Fine, it's your party. But talk to the people who built it before you move it.
Some of us joined for what the manifesto said. I hope you know what you're trading it for.
figure_quit: That's a good person gone. I'd like to know whose turn it is next.
When people like that leave, it isn't because of the coffee.
hypocrisy: You told a hall full of people the elites are robbing them. Then you cashed the elites' cheque. I keep both the speech and the receipt.
We can be against the people at the top, or we can take their money. Not both. Not for long.
deny: You denied it. We both know what's in the files. I hope whoever wrote that denial has a good lawyer.
A denial is a bet that nobody has the papers. Somebody always has the papers.
scapegoat: You put a colleague in front of the bus and paid for the ticket. The people who built this party were watching.
I've worked with them for years. They didn't deserve that, and you know it.
